Only the reach between Aydhab and Suakin, the one eastern holding the page gives (for the 14th century), is left for this one year; the move into Maris is undated and drawn from 1175, the year the Ayyubid hold of Qasr Ibrim ends (Makuria /ledger/5). Revised 2026-11-01 (fx-25): the Sudanese Red Sea state is no longer drawn for 1174. The Banu Kanz page gives 'the region between the Red Sea ports of Aydhab and Suakin' only in the account of the 1365 Mamluk expedition (no earlier year), while the Alodia dossier holds that coast from c. 950 (Alodia page: 'the Eastern Desert along the Red Sea coast'); the two bridges collided on 624 cells in 1174, 1175 and 1365. Only the Aydhab disc is kept here.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, redrawn after review. The first draft kept Aswan's countryside and the whole Egyptian Eastern Desert to 1365, but the Banu Kanz page has the Banu Kanz lose Aswan in 1174 and move south into Maris, with the Hawwara replacing them later, and the 14th-century page text gives them only "the region between the Red Sea ports of Aydhab and Suakin". Drawn now: Maris (Lower Nubia without the Aswan district, about 45,000 km2) plus the Sudanese Red Sea state and an Aydhab disc (about 0.2 M km2). The eastern reach is the page's only eastern statement and is carried back to 1175 as a bridge. In 1317 a Kanz al-Dawla seized the Makurian throne, which is a change of dynasty in Makuria, not drawn as Banu Kanz land. The Makuria page has the Banu Kanz "finally expelled from Aswan in 1412/3" and intermarrying "as far south as Wadi es-Sebua", which does not fit a state that ended in 1365; the infobox dissolution of 1365 is kept. No area on the page. Revised 2026-11-01 (fx-25): (1) Maris is drawn only north of 22.9 N, 21 cells: the Banu Kanz page puts Maris in 'northern Nubia' and gives no extent, and the Makuria page (opened 2026-11-01) has the Makurian army at 'Adindan near Faras' in 1175, Qasr Ibrim returning to Makuria that year, and the court at Gebel Adda after 1365, all south of 22.9 N; the old Lower Nubia disc took 156 cells from Makuria with no page behind it. (2) The Sudanese Red Sea state is dropped before 1365, as in the 1174 keyframe.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (review repair 2026-10-19). 1365: Dongola falls and its king is killed (Makuria page: "In 1365, a civil war ended with the loss of Dongola"; the Banu Kanz page: Dongola "was captured by the tribesmen and its king killed"), then the chiefs surrender in December. The Makuria page names the Banu Ja'd, not the Banu Kanz, for the killing of the king, so the actor is a reading (confidence 2). Revised 2026-11-01 (fx-25): Maris is the same 21-cell Aswan side of Lower Nubia as in the 1175 keyframe; the Red Sea reach comes in by the new 1365 gain (ledger) from Alodia.

ledger.note: 1174: Aswan lost to the Ayyubids; the Banu Kanz move south. "The Ayyubid army proceeded to confront the Banu Kanz, who were defeated after major clashes in Aswan"; "The expulsion of the Banu Kanz from the frontier zone around Aswan caused the area's neglect"; "With the loss of their capital, the Banu Kanz migrated south to occupy Maris". The page dates the insurrection to 1174 and gives no separate year for the defeat (confidence 2, not 3); the Eastern Desert north of Aydhab is my reading of what went with Aswan. Egypt in 1174 is the Fatimid Caliphate row of Cliopatria (911..1176), the Ayyubid Sultanate row starts in 1177; the ayyubid-sultanate dossier of me-09 should carry the matching gain.

ledger.note: After 1174: the Banu Kanz move south into Maris. "With the loss of their capital, the Banu Kanz migrated south to occupy Maris" (Banu Kanz page); the page gives no year, only that Nubian control of the region "had been significantly diminished due to the Ayyubid punitive expedition in 1172". 1175 is a bridge, the year the Ayyubid hold of Qasr Ibrim ends (Makuria /ledger/5; Makuria page: "until in 1175 a Nubian army finally arrived to confront the invaders at Adindan near Faras"). No mirror loss in makuria: the Makuria page, re-read 2026-10-19, never uses the name Maris, does not mention the Banu Kanz before 1317 and does not say Makuria lost Lower Nubia to anyone in the 1170s, so the af-01-a dossier has nothing to answer this gain with. The counterpart stays makuria because the Banu Kanz page calls Maris land of "Nubian control"; af-01-a could add a confidence 1 loss in 1175 if it agrees. Revised 2026-11-01 (fx-25): the region is now the 21-cell Aswan side of Lower Nubia (north of 22.9 N); makuria carries the mirror loss (ledger, 1175, confidence 1).

ledger.note: By December 1365: the Banu Kanz and Banu Ikrima hold the Red Sea reach (mirror loss in alodia). Banu Kanz page, opened 2026-11-01: the Banu Kanz and Banu Ikrima were 'in control of the region between the Red Sea ports of Aydhab and Suakin' in the account of the Mamluk expedition that followed the capture of Dongola, and 'The Kanz al-Dawla and other chiefs surrendered to the Mamluk governor of Qus in December 1365.' The page gives no earlier date for this control and no handover from Alodia; the event is placed at the latest year the page shows it, so the Sudanese Red Sea hills are not Banu Kanz land before 1365. Added fx-25 to settle 624 cells that alodia and banu-kanz both claimed in 1174, 1175 and 1365.

1365: Dongola falls to the tribesmen. Makuria page: "in 1365 an unnamed nephew of the king allied with the Banu Ja'd tribe to kill his uncle in battle and seize the throne" and "In 1365, a civil war ended with the loss of Dongola"; Banu Kanz page: "The Mamluks sent an expedition against the Banu Kanz and Banu Ikrima after Dongola was captured by the tribesmen and its king killed", with the Banu Kanz and Banu Ikrima "in control of the region between the Red Sea ports of Aydhab and Suakin" (no year on the Banu Kanz page; the surrender is December 1365). Year from the Makuria page; the Makuria page names the Banu Ja'd for the killing, the Banu Kanz page the 'tribesmen' of the Banu Kanz and Banu Ikrima, so which tribe held Dongola is a reading. Mirrors makuria /ledger/8.

ledger.note: December 1365: the Banu Kanz surrender to the Mamluks. "The Kanz al-Dawla and other chiefs surrendered to the Mamluk governor of Qus in December 1365"; infobox "Dissolution: 1365". The page still has the Banu Kanz attack Aswan in 1366 and 1370 and be defeated in 1378 by Ibn Hassan, the governor of Aswan. The page names the surrender, not the land: Maris and the Aydhab-Suakin reach are my reading. The Dongola reach is not handed to the Mamluks, who "returned to Egypt right after, in early 1366" without reconquering Dongola (Makuria page).

wars.outcome: A Nubian army with former Fatimid African contingents sacked Aswan in 1171/72; Saladin sent an expedition in 1172 that reduced Nubian control of Maris; in 1174 the Ayyubids defeated Ibn al-Mutawwaj's Fatimid-restoring uprising at Aswan.
wars.note: The Banu Kanz first asked Saladin for help, then rose against him in 1174.

wars.name: Mamluk expeditions against the Banu Kanz
wars.outcome: Two Mamluk expeditions failed, the last in 1324; the Kanz al-Dawla surrendered in December 1365; raids on Aswan in 1366 and 1370 and a defeat in 1378.
wars.note: The page dates only the last expedition (1324). In 1317 the Mamluks arrested the Kanz al-Dawla, a nephew of King Karanbas of Makuria; he was released and seized the Makurian throne.

certainty.note: Desert and river frontier of Upper Egypt with Nubia; no line given.

sources.title: Banu Kanz
sources.note: Founded 943 (Ishaq ibn Bishr), Kanz al-Dawla title 1006, Ayyubid expedition 1172-74, migration to Maris, Makurian throne 1317, Mamluk expeditions to 1324, surrender December 1365. Territory: Aswan, the Nubian frontier, the Eastern Desert to the Red Sea. Re-read 2026-10-19: defeat at Aswan and the move to Maris (undated), Dongola captured by the tribesmen (undated), the Aydhab-Suakin reach, attacks on Aswan 1366 and 1370, defeat 1378.

sources.title: Makuria
sources.note: Read for the repair: Qasr Ibrim taken January 1173 and the Ayyubid raids end 1175 at Adindan; 1365 civil war, loss of Dongola, the Banu Ja'd and the Mamluk return in early 1366; Banu Kanz expelled from Aswan 1412/3; no mention of Maris.

notes:
New dossier: Cliopatria lacks the Banu Kanz. One page opened (Banu Kanz; budget 1-2). Thin on land: only the territory list and undated 'migrated south to occupy Maris'. The makuria dossier (af-01-a) cites 'banu-kanz' as counterpart for Dongola in 1365 ('controlled the area from Aydhab and Suakin west to the Nile'): that sentence was not on the page text returned in this run, so no event here moves Dongola. Not settled: the Banu Kanz's relation to the Fatimids (governor reporting to the Fatimid governor of Qus: the lord's vassal event belongs to the Fatimid dossier), the 1317 episode (a Kanz al-Dawla takes the Makurian throne), the date the Banu Kanz left Aswan (1412/3 on the Makuria page). Slug 'beja' (predecessor, Hadariba Beja) is proposed by af-01-a and not written here. Gazetteer: all names resolved.
Predecessor: the Rabi'ah-Hadariba principality of Ishaq ibn Bishr, who succeeded his maternal Beja uncles in 943; the Beja have no dossier here (the Beja page dates only al-Ya'qubi's six 9th-century kingdoms between Aswan and Massawa), so identity.predecessors is empty. fx-25 (2026-11-01): Maris narrowed to the 21-cell Aswan side of Lower Nubia (the Makuria page keeps Qasr Ibrim, Gebel Adda and Adindan Makurian) and the Sudanese Red Sea hills drawn only from 1365 (new gain from alodia); makuria and alodia carry the mirror losses.
